title: John Chrysostom on 1 Samuel 1:13
body: “But observe even after this her deep reverence. "Only her lips moved, but her voice," it saith, "was not heard." (1 Sam.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon

title: Basil the Great on 1 Samuel 9:3
body: “So six mss. Editors have substituted "enemies." The letter does not exist in the Codex Harlæanus. Onoi is supposed to mean that Faustinus and John, the predecessors of Amphilochius in the see of Iconium, were not very wise bishops.”
author: Basil the Great, Hexaemeron

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Samuel 10:21
body: “It seems necessary to state what are meant by "families." (patriai) Here on earth, indeed there are "families" that is races sprung from one parent stock; but in heaven how can this be, where none is born of another?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Samuel 12:23
body: “But, as I said, if we be active also ourselves, the prayers for us avail too. Hear Paul saying, "For I know that this shall turn to my salvation, through your supplication, and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ." (Philip.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Samuel 24:13
body: “There is no authority for a different reading, but it seems to be rightly conjectured by Savile and Ben.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Samuel 24:17
body: “The meaning which is here attached to the expression: thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, viz.: thou shalt bring the divine vengeance upon him, is very improbable.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans

title: Augustine on 1 Samuel 28:7
body: “Ventriloqua femina. The woman with a familiar spirit to whom Saul resorted in his extremity is called in the Septuagint translation engastrimuthos.”
author: Augustine, The City of God
